title: Admins can switch the Database creation rights
summary: Two team switches decide who may create Database entries and who may create and edit Modules.
details: In Admin panel, Team, the Database sub-heading has two switches: Allow users to create Database entries, and Allow users to create and edit Modules. Both are on by default.
With Modules on, any user of the team can create and edit a module. Turn it off and only admins can. Deleting a module stays with admins, and your personal modules are not affected.
Turn Create Database entries off and the New entry button is hidden for people who are not admins. Who can read or edit an entry does not change.
The Database list itself is unchanged.
imageAlt: Admin panel, Team tab: the Database card with the two switches Allow users to create Database entries and Allow users to create and edit Modules

title: The Database in the guide, with an "i" where you need it
summary: Five new guide cards explain the Database, its storage, the sequence editor, the family tree and who can edit. A small i opens each one from the place it is about.
details: The guide has a Database area: modules and entries, storage with boxes and tubes, the sequence editor, the family tree, and who can edit, folders and personal modules.

Click the small i beside the Database title and Dashboard, the Sequence, Primers and probes, Lineage and Storage headings of an entry, the Storage browser, Add container, Modules, the Database settings of Admin, and the Who can edit and My modules boxes.
The New entry window has an i that opens the Database guide in a new tab.
On the personal module of a colleague that you only look at, the New entry button is no longer shown, since you cannot add to it.
imageAlt: The top of the Database page with the module tabs and the small i beside the Database title, outlined

title: Database and modules
summary: A shared catalogue of what your lab keeps (plasmids, antibodies, cells, primers and more), one module for each kind.
details: fa-database::Open Database in the top bar. Each kind of thing is a module, shown as a tab: Plasmids, Antibodies, Primers and so on.
fa-plus::The blue New entry button under the tabs adds an entry to the module you are in. In Plasmids it asks for a name, parents and a sequence.
fa-table-list::The table has the columns of the module. Type under a heading to filter, press Columns to choose them, the arrow opens a row in place.
fa-user::All entries shows the lab Database; My entries shows yours, also those without a number. A yellow bar on an entry offers Register.
fa-id-card::An entry has Details, Sequence, Storage, Lineage, Activity, Links and Permissions. Everyone reads; the owner and admins change it.
fa-file-import::Import adds entries from a file and Export saves the list, both above the table.
imageAlt: The Database page with the Plasmids module open: the module tabs, the New entry: Plasmids button and the table of plasmids with a filter under each heading
purpose: Find any plasmid, antibody or sample, see what it is and where it is kept, and add new ones the same way every time.
uses: Keep a Plasmids module with the backbone, insert and resistance in columns of their own.
Filter a module by one column to find every entry with the same value.
Make a new entry privately first, then register it when it is ready.
news: New: a separate Database for what your lab keeps, with its own modules, numbers, storage and sequence tools.
shot: The Database page with a module open, its tabs, the New entry button and the table

screenshots.caption: An entry: the module and its own number, the Details fields and the Sequence section

title: Storage: boxes, slots and tubes
summary: Record where everything is kept: rooms, freezers, racks and boxes, with every tube in its own slot.
details: fa-box-open::Open Storage browser in the Database menu. The tree has the tabs Lab storage, My storage and Other storage, with a search.
fa-plus::Add a location creates a place: a location, fridge, freezer, rack or box. Open a place to rename, change or move it with its contents.
fa-table-cells::A box has slots: set its size and the grid shows every slot. A tube shows the name of its entry.
fa-vial::To store a tube, open the entry and press Add storage in its Storage section: choose the place, how many tubes and how much in each.
fa-hand-pointer::Drag a tube to a free slot to move it. Cmd/Ctrl-click or Shift-click free slots to fill several at once.
fa-user-shield::Anyone who can read an entry can add, move or remove its tubes. Only admins delete a place.
imageAlt: The Storage browser: the tree of places on the left and, for Freezer -80 A, its racks with two boxes filled and free places outlined, and the count of racks and slots
purpose: Find a tube in seconds and know how much is left, without a spreadsheet of freezer positions.
uses: Put each freezer, rack and box in the tree, so the page of a plasmid says exactly which box and slot to open.
Move a whole rack to another freezer in one step.
Fill a new box by dragging over its free slots and adding tubes to them.
news: New: places, boxes with slots, and tubes you can drag from slot to slot.
shot: A storage box with a grid of slots and tubes in blue

screenshots.caption: A box opened in the Storage browser: every slot of the 9 by 9 grid, with a tube named after its entry in the filled ones

title: Sequence editor, reads and primers
summary: Open the sequence of a plasmid in a full editor, align sequencing reads to it, and keep its primers with its orders.
details: fa-dna::A plasmid with a .gb, .gbk, .fasta or .dna file shows a Sequence section. Press the file: circular and linear map, sequence, cut sites.
fa-floppy-disk::A change saves by itself as a new version and the earlier ones are kept. A registered plasmid is locked: unlock it to edit.
fa-plus::Add a sequence in the New entry window of Plasmids or on a plasmid's edit page. Tools > Sequence editor opens an empty editor.
fa-screwdriver-wrench::The tool rail on the right has Primers and probes, Design primers, Compare digests, Find and add features and Version history.
fa-align-left::Attach .ab1 reads and press Alignment of sequencing reads: they are aligned to the plasmid with their traces under them.
fa-vial::Primers are entries of the Primers module: attach them to a plasmid, see where they bind and send chosen ones to an order.
imageAlt: The sequence editor on a plasmid: the circular map with its features, the sequence with the CMV promoter, and the tool rail on the right
purpose: Work on a plasmid map and its sequencing results next to its page, without exporting files to another program.
uses: Open a plasmid, look at its cut sites and choose enzymes for a diagnostic digest.
Drop the .ab1 files of a sequencing run on the Align tool and see where a read differs from the map.
Send three primers to an order and have the supplier sheet attached for you.
news: New: a sequence editor, alignment of reads and a primers tool built into the Database.
shot: The sequence editor with a circular map, the sequence and the tool rail

title: Family tree: parents and daughters
summary: Record what each construct was made from and what was made from it, and see the whole family as a tree.
details: fa-sitemap::The Lineage section has Parents and Daughters. Type in Add a parent or Add a daughter, pick an entry; the cross removes a link.
fa-diagram-project::The Family tree draws the entry in the middle, its ancestors above and its descendants below. The names are links.
fa-copy::A copy made with Copy in the list or Duplicate in the toolbar becomes a daughter of the original.
fa-user-pen::You need edit rights to change the parents of an entry, and a link that makes an entry descend from itself is refused.
imageAlt: The Lineage section of a plasmid: its two parents, the daughters box and the family tree with the plasmid in the middle
purpose: Keep track of where each clone comes from, so you can always trace it back to the plasmids it was built from.
uses: Link a finished construct to the backbone and the insert it was cloned from.
Open a backbone and see every construct that was made from it.
Duplicate a plasmid to start a new version and have the link made for you.
news: New: parents, daughters and a family tree for the entries of the Database.
shot: The Lineage section with parents, daughters and the family tree

title: Who can edit, folders and personal modules
summary: Let colleagues edit your entries, organise the Database in its own folders, and keep modules of your own.
details: fa-user-pen::Who can edit: in Permissions on the edit page, the owner adds people or groups who may edit too. The list has Who can edit… for many.
fa-folder-tree::The Database has folders of its own, in the Folders tab of the sidebar while you are in the Database. File entries there; filter by folder.
fa-user-lock::My modules… in the Database menu makes a module only you see. Its entries get your own My_id and no number of the lab.
fa-magnifying-glass::Browse someone's modules… adds a colleague's personal module read-only for 30 minutes. The owner sees who looked.
fa-id-badge::Register in the lab Database gives an entry the ID of the lab; Register for myself gives it your own My_id and keeps it private.
imageAlt: The Who can edit window of an entry: the groups, a list of people to tick and Everyone in the team
purpose: Share the work on an entry with the people who need it, and keep your own working space apart from the lab’s database.
uses: Give the people of one project edit access to its plasmids with a group.
Try a new kind of record in a module of your own before you propose it to the lab.
Let a collaborator look at your Primers module for half an hour.
news: New: owners can let others edit, the Database has its own folders, and everyone can have modules of their own.
shot: The Who can edit window of an entry
